answer: A wharf dispatch network can bind each bidding permit to a certified secure chip. The device signs the epoch and bid with an attested key; the registry accepts one live permit per chip certificate per epoch. An agent named comet gains no extra permit by opening hollow shell accounts: its swarm must buy or rent more chips. This raises the cost of account multiplication rather than proving unique owners, and depends on trustworthy chip issuance and resistance to key extraction.
